title: k-error linear complexity of an Euler-quotient pq-squared sequence
summary: Determine the complete k-error linear-complexity profile of the source-defined binary sequence derived from Euler quotients modulo pq.

formal_statement.body: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct odd primes with $p\mid(q-1)$ and $2^{q-1}\not\equiv1\pmod{q^2}$, and let $s$ be the source-defined binary threshold sequence of period $pq^2$ derived from Euler quotients modulo $pq$. Determine $L_k(s)$ exactly for every admissible $(p,q,k)$, including whether $L_1(s)=L(s)$ throughout the full parameter family.

scope.domain: Binary pq-squared-periodic threshold sequences derived from Euler quotients
assumptions: $s$ is the exact source-defined binary threshold sequence
parameters: $k$: number of altered terms per period
scope.unresolved_remainder: The exact k-error profile remains unknown for the full admissible (p,q,k) family, including the experimentally emphasized k=1 stability claim. Results for other Euler-quotient sequence families do not cover this source sequence.

citations.label: Zhang--Gao--Zhao, Euler-quotient pq-squared sequences
citations.locator: Concluding Remarks, journal p. 5779; k=1 experiment, journal p. 5775

progress.summary: The source explicitly leaves the full k-error linear complexity open and reports experiments suggesting stability at k=1.
